facts.text: Royal Oak earned its name in 1819 when Governor Lewis Cass saw a lone oak tree that reminded him of the Royal Oak where King Charles II hid.
Since the 1930s, extensive tree‑planting has turned Royal Oak into Michigan’s “City of Trees,” though recent development sparks debate over forest upkeep.
Commuter rail ran from Pontiac to downtown Detroit with two stops in Royal Oak until October 17, 1983, when the service ended.
The Shrine of the Little Flower, built in 1929, dominates Royal Oak’s skyline with its 130‑foot Art Deco tower.
In 2022, the Royal Oak City Commission approved demolition of the historic Main Art Theater, once a beloved movie‑goer landmark.
Royal Oak sits on the Woodward Corridor, intersected by Interstate 75 and Interstate 696, linking it to Detroit’s core.
